name: MKI Guest Pass
overview: Temporary guest accounts from a link, QR code or code: only the libraries you pick, locked and deleted when the pass ends.
description: Create a pass on the settings page, pick the libraries, how long it lasts, how many people can use it, how many devices and streams each of them gets and the highest rating, then send the link, show the QR code or read out the code. A guest opens it, types a first name and is watching a minute later: the plugin creates a hidden guest account with no password and signs it in on that browser. TVs are signed in with Quick Connect from the guest's phone. When the pass ends, playback stops, every device is signed out and the account is locked, then deleted a few days later. Links hold 256 random bits and are stored only as a keyed fingerprint, codes and joins are rate-limited, and guests are never administrators: they cannot see other users, download, delete, change settings, use Seerr or start library scans. Turning the plugin off locks every guest; uninstalling deletes them.
changelog: The join page shows Jellyfin's own logo from your server, and says up front that Jellyfin opens right there, already signed in. A guest who cannot join is never left on the page: each case says why and what to do next, with Try again where it helps. A pass for the home network only, opened from elsewhere, tells the guest to join your Wi-Fi or to ask you, and the new Where action on the pass allows it from anywhere (or limits it to home again) without a new link. The settings page warns when the browser you use counts as away, since a home-network link would not open there, and the share window and invitation say when a pass works at home only. Joining no longer throws the guest back to the sign-in page when an older MKI Password Policy is installed: until it is updated to 1.1.1.0, Guest Pass lets nobody join, and both the join page and the settings page say what to do. A guest whose home-only pass no longer opens where they are is signed out with a note and a way back, instead of a Jellyfin that only shows errors. Home only is stricter. Streams and subtitles are refused away from home too. Narrowing a pass also stops playback on away devices, and a failed change is repaired on its own. Where also works on an ended pass. A known reverse proxy that names no visitor, or names one its X-Real-IP disagrees with, is no longer trusted, and home-only passes are refused where no visitor address can be seen: on a Unix socket, or from the Jellyfin machine itself. The form for a new home-only pass explains what a reverse proxy has to send.
